still confused about what the Unabomber was fighting against.

  Since there is still a lot of confusion about just what the Unabomber Manifesto supports or doesn't support, I am going to post this a collection of "quotable quotes" from the Manifesto which illustrate FC's main focus, which is : human freedom, and fear of future technologies which may take it away. 

   A personal comment: Though some of you get the impression that I wholeheartedly endorse FC's bombing campaign, this isn't the case. When I think about the actual deeds, I am saddened and repulsed as anyone would be. But when I read some of these passages in the manifesto I could not help but feel a weird ambivalence: it was terrible what FC did, yet his rhetoric  is so passionate and fiery that I felt the way a listener in 1776 may have felt when Patrick Henry shouted "give me liberty or give me death". (Those guys were revolutionaries too, and they didn't mean to further their cause with flowers!)
   People brush off the manifesto by saying that FC was a nut with a personal axe to grind. Or that 'you shouldn't listen to him because he's a murderer".Or that "other scholars have written better essays on the subject." Well, to me none of this changes the fact: The way our society is going, these issues ought to be discussed and put before the public consciousness as loudly and as often as possible!

LOSS OF FREEDOM (my own headlines added)
93. Industrial Technological society cannot be reformed in such a way as to prevent it from progressively narrowing the sphere of human freedom. ...by "freedom" we mean the opportunity to go thru the power proccess...without interference from anyone, especially from any large organization. Freedom means having power..to control the circumstances of one's own life.
111. There has been a consistent tendency...for technology to strengthen the system at a high cost in individual freedom and local autonomy...freedom and tecnological progress are incompatible.
114. modern man is strapped down by a network of rules and regulations, and his fate depends on the actions of persons remote from him whose decisions he cannot influence... the result is a sense of powerlessness on the part of the average person.
127. A technological advance that appears not to threaten freedom often turns out to threaten it very seriously later on. For example, consider motorized transport. ..when a new item of technology is introduced as an option that an individual can accept or not as he chooses, it does not necessaryily remain optional.... the new technology changes society in such a way that people eventually find themselves forced to use it.
135  While the industrial system is sick we must destroy it. If we compromise with it and let it recover from its sickness, it will eventually wipe out all of our freedom.

ALTERATION OF HUMAN NATURE
144.  Human nature has in the past put certain limits on the development of societies. People could be pushed only so far and no farther. But today this may be changing, because modern technology is developing ways for modifying human beings
145.    Imagine a society that subjects people to conditions that make them terribly unhappy, then gives them drugs to take away their unhappiness. It is already happening to some extent... techniques of surveillance...methods of propaganda... education...psychological techniques for controlling human behavior...biological methods probably will have to be used. ...Neurology may provide other avenues for modifying the human mind. Genetic engineering of human beings... formerly the limits of human endurance have imposed limits on the deveopment of societies...industrial-tech. coeity will be able to pass those limits by modifying human beings, whether by psychological mthocs or biological methods or both... 

BIOLOGICAL CONTROL OF BEHAVIOR
157. ... it is likely that tecnology will eventually acquire something approaching complete control over human behavior. It has been established...that human thought and behavior have a largely biological basis.  ...the fact that human thoughts and feelings are so open to biological intervnetion shows that the problem of controlling human behavior is mainly a technical problem...the kind of problem that is accessible to scientific attack. Giving the outstanding record of our society in solving tehcnical problems it is overwhelmingly probable that great adavnces will be made in the control of human behavior. Will public resistance prevent the introduction of tech. control? it certainly would if an attempt were made to introduce such control all at once. but since control will be introduced thru a long sequence of small advances, there will be no rational and effective public resistance.
160. To those who think that all this sounds like science fiction, we point out that yesterday's sf is today's fact. the Industrial REvolution has radically altered man's environment and way of life ... as tech. is increasingly applied to to the human body & mind, man himself will be altered as radically as his environment and way of life has been. 

163. suppose the system survives the crisis of the next several decades. by that time it will have solved...the [problem of] "socializing human beings" ...making people sufficiently docile so that their behavior no longer threatens the system. there will be no further obstacle to the development of tech. and it would presumably advance toward its logical conlusion, which is complete control over everything on earth.
Human freedom will have vanished...indivuduals...will be impotent vis a vis large organizations armed with supertech. and an arsenal of advanced psych,. and biological tools for manipulating human beings , besides instrument of surveillance and physical coercion.
167. Is it cruel to work for the breakdown of the system?...one has to balance struggle and death against the loss of freedom & dignity.

INTELLIGENT MACHINES, DOMESTICATED HUMANS
172. let us postulate that ...scientists succed in developing intelligent machines that can do all things better than human beings can do them. ... machines might be permitted to make all of their own decisions without human oversight...  the fate of the human race would be at the mercy of the machines. 
  It is possible that human control  over machines may be retained. due to improved techniques the elite will have great controlover the masses...because human work will no longer be necessary the masses will be superfluous, a useless burden...it the elite is ruthless they may simply decide to exterminate the mass of humanity...or, the elite may play the role of good shepherds...see that everyone's needs are satifsfied...of course life will be so purposeless that people will have to be ...engineered...those engineeredd human beings may be happy... but they most certainly will not be free. They will have been reduced to the status of domestic animals.

HUMAN OBSOLESCENCE: A FUTURE SCENARIO THAT LOOKS FAMILIAR
175. ...there will be an increasing surplus of human workers at the lower levels of ability. On those who are employed, ever increasing demands will be placed. they will need more & more training, more & more ability, will have to be ever more reliable, conforming and docile, because they will be more & more like cells of a giant organism. their tasks will be increasingly specialized so that their work will.. be out of touch with the real world... the system will have to use any means...to enginer people to be docile... the society may find competitiveness useful...we can imagine a furure soceity in which there is endless competition for positions of prestige and power.

177 whatever may be left of wild nature will be reduced to remnants preserved for scientific study and kept under the supervision & management of scientistas. In the long run...it is likely that neither the human race nor any other important organisms wil exist as we know them today...modifications will probably continue until man & other organisms have been utterly transformed.
  It is certain that technology is creating for human beings a new physical & social environment radically different than that to which natural selection has adapted the human race physically & phychologically....

179.   It would be better to dump the whole stinkng system and take the consequences.
